children: Federal Reserve Bank of New York President John Williams said Monday that while the economy’s performance will drive what the central bank does with monetary policy, he’s not ruling out steady rate increases if that’s what’s needed.

“I don't have in my mind a particular timing” when it comes to more US rate hikes, Williams told reporters after a speech before the University of Mount Saint Vincent. “We're going to have to learn along the way as we get more data,” the official said, while noting, “I'm not excluding options” and “I would not exclude, you know, moving at consecutive meetings at all if that was what was needed.”

title: Fed's Williams keeping options open on pace of future US rate hikes
